Appearance:
Shri Bhaskar Agrawal, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Kailash Chandra Waghela, learned counsel for the
 respondent .
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being
aggrieved by the award dated 03.04.2007 in Macc No.119/2005 by 3rd Additional Mact, Ujjain
for exonera
tion of the liability or reduction of compensation

. 
2. Shorn of unnecessary details, facts of the case in brief are that an application under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was preferred claiming compensation of Rs.26,25,000/- regarding death of claimant, 18 years old unmarried son Ramchandra NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:6922 2 MA-1917-2007 who died on 09.03.2004 near the well of Chandersingh situated at Tahsil Badnagar, district Ujjain within the jurisdiction of PS Bhatpachliya, district Ujjain.

3. It is stated that deceased was working as agricultural labourer and on the date of incident he was working as agricultrual labourer on the trailor No.MP-13-KC-1398 attached with the tractor bearing no.MP-13-K-9741 insured with appellant/non applicant no.5.
4.
The claim was replied by respondents No.3 & 6 jointly.

Separate reply was filed by appellant/non applicant no.5 on various grounds including breach of policy conditions with specific plea that at the relevant point of time the offending vehicle was used otherwise than agricultural purposes and trailor was insured only for agricultural purposes.

Tribunal framed issues and recorded the evidence of Madanlal (PW/1) and appellant/non applicant no.5 examined administrative officer Pradeep National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Respondent No. (01) Deceased Madanlal ... on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33614884/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal passed the award and this appeal has been preferred on the ground that Tribunal has not properly considered the fact that deceased was travelling as a passenger in the said tractor trolley whose risk was not covered under the policy and the trolley was insured for the use of agricultural purposes while it was used for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6922 3 MA-1917-2007 transporting boulders which was not an agricultural product.
The tribunal erred in not considering the fact that the insurance company is not statutorily required to cover the risk of deceased.
No extra premium had been taken by the appellant/insurance company.
The appellant relied on Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Brij Mohan and others - 2007 ACJ 1909 (SC).

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Brij Mohan and others - 2007 ACJ 1909 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Heard.
7.
Perused the record.
8. Firstly, we are dealing with the quantum of compensation.
As per para-18 and 19 of the award the deceased was 18 years old and was studying also while working as labourer.
The award has been passed only for a compensation of Rs.1,68,000/-, hence the quantum is very meager, therefore, it does not require interference.

9. Record of the Tribunal discloses that appellant himself has filed Ex.D/2 which is the certified copy of the proceedings in criminal case no.78/2004 of the Court of JMFC, Badnawar, district Ujjain which discloses that driver of offending vehicle was convicted for the offence arising out of this incident, hence negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle does not require further proof and unrebutted testimony of Madan (PW/1) discloses that deceased Ramchandra was pouring manure in the field at the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6922 4 MA-1917-2007 time of incident and that is agricultural operation.
Accordingly, the ground for exoneration does not survive.
The appellant does not succeed on the strength of Brij Mohan (supra).
Thus, this appeal being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
